Drive Team Excellence with Customized Corporate Training on 5G Architecture and Key Principles

5G is rapidly becoming the backbone of next-generation connectivity for enterprises, telecom operators, and industrial deployments. As operators accelerate 5G rollouts and enterprises adopt private 5G, the demand for engineers who can design, plan, and optimise 5G networks has outpaced the available talent pool.

Edstellar's instructor-led corporate training closes that gap quickly, giving your team the architectural depth, hands-on practice, and decision-making fluency to move from awareness to applied competency in a single engagement.

Key Learning Outcomes of 5G Architecture and Key Principles Training Workshop for Employees

Upon successful completion of the training workshop, your team will be able to apply each of the following capabilities to live planning, deployment, and architecture decisions.

Utilise 5G's potential for business innovation and new service models, mapping technology capabilities to measurable business outcomes.

Deploy 5G networks considering key architectural principles across RAN, transport, and core network domains.

Evaluate 5G architecture components and functions including gNB, AMF, SMF, UPF, PCF, UDM, and AUSF.

Enhance network performance and user experience through KPI-driven optimisation, traffic management, and QoS engineering.

Identify diverse 5G use cases across industries, smart manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, and smart cities.

Comprehend the concept and application of network slicing in 5G, including eMBB, URLLC, and mMTC slice types.

Design and implement 5G core network functions using service-based architecture (SBA) principles and service-based interfaces (SBI).

Apply 5G security frameworks per 3GPP TS 33.501, authentication, ciphering, key hierarchy, and identity privacy.

Interpret 5G RAN architecture including numerology, mmWave and sub-6 GHz spectrum, massive MIMO, and beamforming.

Variant A · Curriculum only

Topics and Outline of 5G Architecture and Key Principles Training

Eight modules across 16 to 24 instructor-led hours. Each module combines theoretical frameworks, architecture diagrams, and hands-on lab exercises. Click any module to explore its topics and the artefact your team will build.

Reviewed by Industry Practitioners
Curriculum validated by OEM & Tier-1 engineers

Introduction to 5G Services and Architecture

2 – 3 Hours
  • History and evolution of 5G from 1G through 4G predecessors
  • The need for 5G, data demand, IoT, low latency, and high reliability use cases
  • Performance requirements, URLLC, mMTC, and eMBB service categories
  • Sub-systems of a 5G network, RAN, Core, User Equipment (UE)
  • NSA vs SA deployment options and hybrid approaches
  • Virtualisation in 5G, NFV and Software-Defined Networking (SDN)

What Your Team Will Build

Sketch a high-level 5G architecture for a target use case (smart manufacturing or smart city) showing RAN, transport, core, and application layers.

Radio Access Network (RAN)

3 – 4 Hours
  • Numerologies, frequency rates, modulations (QPSK, 16-QAM, 64-QAM), FDD and TDD
  • MIMO, SU-MIMO, MU-MIMO, and beamforming techniques in 5G
  • 5G spectrum, mmWave, sub-6 GHz, spectrum auctions and regulations
  • Dual connectivity, flexible numerology, mini-slot and preemptive scheduling
  • NR (New Radio) cell characteristics, cell ID, and configuration
  • RRC states (Idle, Connected, Inactive) and UE management

What Your Team Will Build

Design an RF plan for a mixed mmWave and sub-6 GHz deployment, including gNB placement, beamforming configuration, and coverage prediction.

Data Flow and Mobility Management

2 – 3 Hours
  • Making the mobile core network more flexible through NFV and virtualisation
  • How an SMF (Session Management Function) controls a UPF (User Plane Function)
  • Dynamic data path management and user plane data routing
  • Setting up PDU sessions in 5G, creation, establishment, configuration
  • Attaching a 5G terminal, registration, authentication, session establishment

What Your Team Will Build

Trace a complete 5G registration and PDU session establishment flow showing signalling between UE, gNB, AMF, SMF, and UPF.

5G Security

2 – 3 Hours
  • Importance and strong aspects of 5G security, CIA triad in 5G context
  • Network functions in charge of security and threat mitigation
  • Identity concealment, identifying a UE without transmitting permanent identity
  • 5G AKA (Authentication and Key Agreement) vs 4G authentication
  • Ciphering, integrity control, and key hierarchy differences between 4G and 5G
  • Diffie-Hellman key exchange for secure communication establishment

What Your Team Will Build

Conduct a 5G security assessment against 3GPP TS 33.501, identifying authentication, integrity, and confidentiality gaps in a sample architecture.

Network Slicing and Use Cases

2 – 3 Hours
  • Introduction to network slicing, definition, benefits, and 5G-specific capabilities
  • Network slice types, eMBB, URLLC, mMTC slice profiles and isolation requirements
  • Creating and managing network slices, lifecycle management and resource allocation
  • Use cases and verticals, industrial automation, healthcare, smart cities, IoT
  • End-to-end QoS mapping across RAN, transport, and core per slice

What Your Team Will Build

Design three network slices (eMBB, URLLC, mMTC) for a manufacturing facility, specifying bandwidth, latency, and reliability targets for each.

5G Core

2 – 3 Hours
  • Network functions, role, importance, and core network services
  • Protocol stack for Service-Based Interface (SBI), layers and communication
  • 5G core overview, service-based architecture, functions, components
  • Network slicing in the core, virtual networks, isolation, resource allocation
  • Core network functions, AMF, SMF, UPF, NRF, NSSF, PCF, UDM, AUSF, NEF
  • NFV, centralised vs distributed deployment, third-party service integration

What Your Team Will Build

Map a complete 5G core architecture showing service-based interfaces, listing each NF (AMF, SMF, UPF, PCF, UDM) and its role.

5G Core Services and Integration

1 – 2 Hours
  • Introduction to 5G core services and key service-based architecture (SBA) principles
  • Service exposure through APIs for external applications
  • Integration with legacy networks, interworking with 4G/LTE
  • Dual connectivity and seamless handover scenarios
  • End-to-end service orchestration and network automation

What Your Team Will Build

Create a 5G service exposure plan showing how external applications access core network capabilities (location, QoS, slice selection) via standard APIs.

5G Applications and Future Trends

1 – 2 Hours
  • Emerging 5G applications, AR, VR, edge computing, and IoT innovations
  • Transforming industries, healthcare, telemedicine, smart manufacturing, Industry 4.0
  • Envisioning a connected future, smart cities, autonomous vehicles, transportation
  • Anticipating future trends, continuous evolution of 5G and the 6G horizon

What Your Team Will Build

Create a business case deck for a vertical-specific 5G deployment (healthcare, logistics, or utilities) with TCO, ROI, and deployment roadmap.

Perform RF propagation modelling and gNB site planning for a 5G mmWave deployment in a dense urban environment.

mmWave RF Planning Coverage

Read brief

Conduct a security assessment of a 5G architecture against 3GPP TS 33.501, identifying gaps and recommending mitigations.

Intermediate 4-5 hrs
Read brief

Evaluate a sample 5G SA architecture for authentication, integrity protection, confidentiality, and privacy controls. Map findings against 3GPP TS 33.501, produce an audit checklist with risk ratings, and propose a prioritised remediation roadmap.

Prerequisites for 5G Architecture and Key Principles Training

Your team should arrive with a basic working understanding of telecommunications and networking. No prior 5G experience is required, the course is structured to take participants from foundational awareness to applied architecture competency.

Telecommunications Fundamentals

Understanding of basic telecom concepts including signal propagation, frequency bands, and network topologies. Prior exposure to LTE or 4G networks is beneficial.

Basic Required

IP Networking Concepts

Familiarity with IP networking layers, routing protocols, and the OSI/TCP-IP model. Ability to read basic network diagrams and understand packet-switched communication.

Basic Required

RF and Wireless Basics

Basic awareness of radio frequency principles, antenna concepts, and wireless communication standards. Useful for understanding 5G spectrum and RAN design decisions.

Helpful, Not Required

Skill Progression: Entry → Exit

5G Architecture Aware → Advanced
Network Slicing None → Advanced
RAN & Core Design Basic → Advanced
Use Case Identification Basic → Intermediate+
Performance Optimisation Basic → Intermediate+
Business Innovation Basic → Intermediate

Frequently Asked Questions About Corporate Group Training for 5G Architecture and Key Principles

What L&D leaders, training buyers, and procurement teams ask before booking a private group cohort.

The programme covers the complete 5G NR architecture stack, RAN (gNB), 5G core network functions (AMF, SMF, UPF, PCF, UDM, AUSF), network slicing, spectrum principles across sub-6 GHz and mmWave, key 5G use cases (eMBB, URLLC, mMTC), and 5G security frameworks per 3GPP TS 33.501. Your team also explores NSA vs SA deployment trade-offs through hands-on capstone projects.

The programme targets telecom engineers, network architects, system engineers, network planners, solutions architects, IT consultants, R&D engineers, technical sales engineers, field engineers, pre-sales engineers, and engineering managers. Mixed-role cohorts are common, the trainer layers content depth so each role gets what they need.

No prior 5G experience is required. A basic understanding of telecommunications, IP networking, and the OSI/TCP-IP model is sufficient. Familiarity with LTE or 4G is helpful but not mandatory. The curriculum brings participants from foundational awareness to applied architecture competency in a single engagement.

The standard duration is 16 to 24 hours spread across two to three days. Custom durations can be arranged for teams requiring focused modules, security-only, RAN-only, or core-only, or extended deep-dives into specific architecture components your team is actively deploying.

Each participant receives an Edstellar certificate of completion with a unique course code and trainer signature. Training content aligns with 3GPP Release 15, 16, and 17 standards and supports preparation for vendor-specific certifications such as Ericsson EACS and Nokia NSP.

Corporate group training is a private engagement delivered exclusively for your team. The curriculum, examples, and labs are tailored to your organisation's deployment scenarios, and every participant in the cohort comes from your company. Discussions stay confidential and the conversation is anchored to your real architecture, unlike open enrollment where participants come from many companies and content stays generic.

Yes. Edstellar offers onsite group training at your office, lab, or meeting space, plus virtual and off-site (third-party venue) options. All three formats include hands-on labs, live Q&A with the trainer, and the same trainer credentials regardless of delivery mode.

Yes. Edstellar tailors examples, lab exercises, and capstone projects to your team's vertical and technology stack, private 5G manufacturing, healthcare, smart cities, Tier-1 telco operator scenarios, and so on. Customisation is part of the engagement, not an extra line item on the invoice.

Group training is priced per cohort, not per seat. Your team can scale without your invoice scaling linearly. Custom curriculum work, language support, and venue costs are quoted upfront in the proposal. There are no surprise extras after the engagement starts.

Beyond the workshop, your team gets access to the Edstellar skills-intelligence platform, monthly office-hour Q&A with the trainer for three months, a private Slack channel for cohort peers and trainer, quarterly refresher modules covering new 3GPP releases, and optional follow-on coaching engagements for senior engineers.
